view: The arithmetic of the guide does not work, and the consensus has not admitted it. 1H26 revenue was $43.9m (Q1 $20.9m, Q2 $23.0m; 10-Q 2026-08-11). The bottom of the $99-103m guide therefore needs $55.1m in 2H, about $27.5m a quarter. My own rebuild of Q3: orthobiologics ex-HEMOBLAST about $16-16.5m (Q1 $15.6m, Q2 about $15.9m), plus HEMOBLAST at the 'more than $1m a month gross' run-rate, about $2.5-3.3m with management's own buffer for Dilon-shipped (net) orders, plus spinal implants about $5.3-5.7m (Q1 $5.3m, Q2 $5.7m), plus perhaps a small BioHorizons dental stocking order. That puts Q3 near $24-26.5m, central about $25m: roughly in line with the $25.5m consensus or slightly below. It would leave Q4 needing about $30m to reach even the bottom of the guide. That is implausible, because Q4 2025 ($32.3m derived) showed no seasonal lift over Q3 2025 ($33.3m), and amnio wound care is still collapsing (MiMedx Q3 2026 wound sales down about 71% on the 2026 Medicare framework). A guide cut, or a withdrawal, is likely; I put it near 70-75%. Liquidity is thin as well: $9.9m cash and $0.7m of revolver availability at June 30, the minimum net revenue covenant waived for both Q4 2025 and Q2 2026, and 1H operating cash burn of $9.4m. A further waiver or tighter liquidity would show in the 10-Q. Against that, the price has already done much of the work. The stock has bled 40% since the Q2 release with no news, it trades near 0.5x EV/sales at its low, and the setup is retail-prone: 77m shares traded on the 2026-08-28 dental headline. Sequential revenue growth of around 10% plus a 'HEMOBLAST now booked gross' story could be spun into a relief bounce. My net read: down is more likely than up, at around 60%, but not at the conviction needed to call it.
unpriced: The sell side still models the full-year guide ($99.4m consensus against a guide that needs about $27.5m a quarter in 2H after a $23.0m Q2), so a guide cut would be a miss against published numbers. That is a stale-estimate blind spot on a thinly covered name. How much of it the 40% post-Q2 slide already holds cannot be shown either way.

recommendation.reason: The guide arithmetically requires about $27.5m a quarter in 2H against a Q3 build near $25m, and consensus ($99.4m FY) still sits at the guide, so a cut is likely and would land inside the window at the bmo release and 8:30 call. But the stock has already fallen about 40% since the Q2 print to a 52-week low at roughly 0.5x EV/sales, and it is retail-prone, so the cut may be largely priced and a relief bounce is a live alternative. That is not enough for a 65% directional call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue of $27m or more with HEMOBLAST booked gross at $3m or more and the FY guide held or only trimmed to about $97m+, which would read as an inflection and likely lift the stock double digits; conversely a going-concern note or an equity raise would make the downside large.

self_critique: The 40% slide since the Q2 print and a 0.5x EV/sales valuation probably already discount a guide cut well below consensus. In a $40k-a-day microcap, the reaction depends more on the headline framing (sequential growth, HEMOBLAST booked gross, the dental launch) than on the sell-side model, so a beat against a depressed price is entirely possible. The Q3 consensus figure itself is uncertain ($25.5m vs $27m).
